questions.questionHtml: Find the sum of the numbers between 550 and 700 such that when they are divided by 12, 16 and 24, leave remainder 5 in each case.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: d

→ LCM of 12, 16, and 24 = 48

Multiple of 48 bigger than 550 which leaves remainder 5 are

→ 1st Number = 48 x 12 + 5 = 581

→ 2nd Number = 48 x 13 + 5 = 629

→ 3rd Number = 48 x 14 + 5 = 677

Sum of these numbers are = 581 + 629 + 677 = 1887

Hence, the sum of the numbers are 1887.

questions.question: Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it seems to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions is true based on the given statement. Statement: H ≤ K = Q < P ≤ T ≥ B Conclusion: I. H ≤ T II. B < P III. K < T IV. P ≥ H
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it seems to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions is true based on the given statement.

Statement: H ≤ K = Q < P ≤ T ≥ B

Conclusion:

I. H ≤ T
II. B < P
III. K < T
IV. P ≥ H

options.text: Only conclusion II and III are true.
options.html: Only conclusion II and III are true.

options.text: Only conclusion I and II are true.
options.html: Only conclusion I and II are true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: c

Only conclusion III is true.

Conclusion I: H ≤ T

We know:
H ≤ K and K < P ≤ T
But we can't directly say H ≤ T since H could be equal to K, and we don't know if K < T or K = T, only that K < P ≤ T.
So H ≤ T is not definitely true

Conclusion II: B < P

We only know:
B ≤ T and P ≤ T
But nothing directly compares B and P, so B < P is not certain.

Similarly, Conclusion IV is also false.

Conclusion III: K < T

From the statement:

K = Q < P ≤ T
So, K < T, Conclusion III is true

Therefore, only conclusion III is true.

You have to consider the statement to be true even it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument. Statement: A black hole is a region of space-time exhibiting gravitational acceleration so strong that nothing – no particles or even electromagnetic radiation such as light – can escape from it. Assumptions: I. No one can come back from a black hole. II. Sun will become a black hole soon.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question, a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument.

Statement: A black hole is a region of space-time exhibiting gravitational acceleration so strong that nothing – no particles or even electromagnetic radiation such as light – can escape from it.

Assumptions:

I. No one can come back from a black hole.

II. Sun will become a black hole soon.

options.text: Both I and II are implicit.
Neither I nor II is implicit.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Only I is implicit.
